title: Picard group of an affine curve as a Jacobian quotient
statement: Let $C$ be a smooth affine connected curve over an algebraically closed field $k$ ([def-sc-curves]), let $\overline C$ be a smooth proper connected curve over $k$ with an open immersion $C\hookrightarrow\overline C$ whose complement $S:=\overline C\setminus C$ is a finite set of closed points ([lem-sc-compactification]), and let $J$ be a Jacobian of $\overline C$ ([def-sc-jacobian], [thm-sc-jacobian-representability]), with the canonical identification $J(k)=\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C)$. Then $S$ is nonempty, and for every point $P_0\in S$ and the subgroup $\Lambda:=\langle [P]-[P_0]:P\in S\rangle\subseteq J(k)$ (classes taken under that identification) there is a group isomorphism $\operatorname{Pic}(C)\cong J(k)/\Lambda$.

proof.text: If the boundary is empty, the open immersion c.i has full opensRange and is an isomorphism (Mathlib isIso_of_isOpenImmersion_of_opensRange_eq_top). The factorization c.comm then makes f proper. By lem-sc-proper-affine-finite its source has topological Krull dimension at most zero, contradicting IsConnectedCurve.krullDim_eq_one from def-sc-curves.

For a boundary point P0, apply Scheme.Hom.pic_restriction_boundary from lem-sc-pic-restriction-boundary to obtain a subgroup H with underlying set picZero, a subgroup Lambda of H whose image under H.subtype is the closure of boundary differences, and a multiplicative equivalence t : H / Lambda -> Pic(C). Since the given G has the same underlying set, H = G; substitute this equality.

Let s be the set of boundary point differences viewed as elements of G. The image G.subtype(s) is exactly the set of boundary point differences in Pic(c.Z): for the reverse inclusion, each such difference is in the closure, hence in the image of Lambda, so has a lift to G. MonoidHom.map_closure and Subgroup.map_injective for the injective subtype show Lambda = closure(s).

Compose the quotient projection G -> G / Lambda with t, obtaining a surjective homomorphism r : G -> Pic(C) with kernel Lambda. Pass to Additive; QuotientAddGroup.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective identifies Additive G / Lambda.toAddSubgroup with Additive Pic(C).

Subgroup.toAddSubgroup_closure and AddMonoidHom.map_closure show that the image of Lambda.toAddSubgroup under e.toAdditive is precisely the closure of the displayed boundary-difference generators in the Jacobian points. QuotientAddGroup.congr transports the quotient along the given equivalence e. Compose it with the inverse of the preceding first-isomorphism equivalence, using quotientAddEquivOfEq for its kernel identification.

lean.statement: theorem IsConnectedCurve.pic_affine_quotient {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsConnectedCurve f] [Smooth f] [IsAffine C] (c : Compactification f) [IsConnectedCurve c.g] [Smooth c.g] [hsm : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 c.g] [GeometricallyIntegral c.g] (hfin : (Set.range c.i.base)ᶜ.Finite) (hcl : ∀ x ∈ (Set.range c.i.base)ᶜ, IsClosed ({x} : Set c.Z)) (J : Over (Spec (.of k))) [CommGrpObj J] [IsJacobian c.g J] (G : Subgroup c.Z.Pic) (hG : (G : Set c.Z.Pic) = c.g.picZero) (e : G ≃* (𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ J)) : (Set.range c.i.base)ᶜ.Nonempty ∧ ∀ (P₀ : closedPoints c.Z), P₀.val ∉ Set.range c.i.base → Nonempty (Additive C.Pic ≃+ Additive (𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ J) ⧸ AddSubgroup.closure {a | ∃ (P : closedPoints c.Z) (L : G), P.val ∉ Set.range c.i.base ∧ L.val = @Scheme.Pic.ofClosedPoint k _ c.Z ⟨c.g⟩ hsm P / @Scheme.Pic.ofClosedPoint k _ c.Z ⟨c.g⟩ hsm P₀ ∧ a = Additive.ofMul (e L)})
